reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Bio: Mario Garza is the artist and researcher behind Symbolic Studies, a project sharing symbolic insights on the zodiac, mythology, folklore and world religions, with astrology as its foundation. A lifelong artist who has worked as an art director and graphic designer for nearly 25 years, he runs Symbolic Studies from the Pacific Northwest alongside his wife Michelle, who co-hosts the podcast with him. His work traces syncretic threads across tarot, occultism and comparative religion, including the argument that the major deities of antiquity were originally polar gods before a solar model was laid over them. He also offers symbolic birth chart and tarot readings, private lessons and freelance design.
reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Name: Mario Garza

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Still Center of the Wheel", "body": "Mario Garza's central claim is that a wheel teaches metaphysics all by itself. The rim stands for action, dispersion and becoming, while the hub stands for unity, stillness and being, so the spiritual journey becomes a movement inward toward your own still center. He points to the unmoved mover, the pole star turning the sky by staying fixed, Buddha meditating inside the dharma wheel, and Christ nailed to the cross as the axis that makes everything else revolve. Chance Garton adds a physics gloss, calling the centripetal draw toward the center going with the flow, and centrifugal flinging the price of fighting it."}, {"title": "A Chariot Fused in Stone", "body": "A long stretch reads the tarot as evidence for that same stillness. Mario notes that the Rider Waite charioteer sits fused in cubic stone, that his sphinxes are seated and not even harnessed to the vehicle, and that older decks draw the wheels crooked and pointed sideways, so the thing cannot roll at all. He reads the Thoth deck's Universe card as hidden ark symbolism, with the fixed creatures spewing flood water under Saturn, and only the bull given swirling eyes. He also traces the major arcana from the Fool as aleph, meaning ox, to the final card as tau."}, {"title": "The Bull at the World Axis", "body": "Both speakers place the bull at the center rather than out on the rim. Mario sets Taurus on the world axis, citing a Vedic bull that occupies the central axial position and arguing that a fixed sign suits something rooted like a tree or a mountain. Chance offers the Buddhist myth of dharma as a bull that loses a leg each age until the iron age leaves it standing on one, then swaps T for D to hear tarma inside Taurus. Mario answers with Ursa Major as the thigh of the bull, plus one legged figures like Mercury and a spinning ballerina."}, {"title": "The Golden Thread of Baal", "body": "Chance calls his linguistic method the golden thread of the bull, built on letter swaps he treats as valid rather than accidental. B trades with V, P with B, L with R and T with D, so the Hebrew par becomes ball, abir reads as father bull, the storm god El carries bull imagery, and the Greek stauros that Jesus hangs on sounds like Tauros with an S in front. He follows the thread into paying a bill, posting bail, the Greek boule as a secret council, and papal bulls, insisting Baal is a title meaning lord rather than a devil."}, {"title": "Poles, Thrones and a Malleable Sky", "body": "The closing turn asks where the center went. Mario says a leader symbolically stands as a pole that gives people orientation, which is why the tarot thrones the High Priestess through the Hierophant before the Lovers breaks the pattern, and why an Egyptian obelisk sits inside a giant keyhole in Vatican Square. Chance argues heliocentric models offer no conceptual center at all, and raises Fomenko's statistical dating of the Almagest to the Renaissance. Mario answers with Christian sky maps and an ancient Chinese zodiac of eight polar constellations later moved onto the ecliptic, suggesting the sky is more malleable than assumed."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: The Dharma wheel. The Christian cross. The Egyptian bull god. Symbolic researcher Mario Garza of Symbolic Studies returns to InnerVerse for a freeform exploration of a central metaphysical pattern, questioning if that pattern may be the architecture of reality itself.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: Why does the Rider-Waite Chariot card show wheels pointed sideways and sphinxes that aren't even harnessed? What does the bull have in common with the cross? Why did nearly every ancient culture place a bull, a tree, or a still point at the center of its cosmology? And what does any of this mean for the spiritual journey in an age of accelerating modernity? Topics traced: the unmoved mover, the still center versus the spinning circumference, bull symbolism across Vedic, Buddhist, Egyptian, Greek, and Phoenician traditions, the philological golden thread connecting wheels, bulls, bills, and lords, René Guénon's reign of quantity, and why "going with the flow" is centripetal physics in metaphysical disguise. The extended conversation follows the wheel and bull symbolism thread into the modern world, tracing the reign of quantity, the acceleration of time, and what ancient metaphysics has to say about the age of AI and digital consciousness.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Reign of Quantity Picks Up Speed", "body": "Mario traces modern acceleration back to Guenon's reign of quantity, where the unified center gives way to dispersion on the rim and every decade churns faster than the last. Chance adds Tracy Twyman's link between money velocity and the felt speed of time, which is why the COVID slowdown made time seem to crawl. Mario's favorite metaphor is the transistor, invented at Bell Labs in 1947, four to a board by the seventies and now trillions in every pocket. From there it gets stranger, since data is also Deva Datta and Buddha becomes bot, and both men wonder whether that circuitry is a body built for something to inhabit."}, {"title": "Tradition at the Center, Modernity on the Rim", "body": "Mario maps the wheel onto history, giving the circumference to modernity and the axle to tradition, so whatever draws you inward is initiatory and whatever flings you outward is counter-initiatory, and what sits on the rim is temporary while the center is eternal. Chance brings in Jack Kelly's reading of Plato, where Atlantis is the pure traditional society and the Republic the perfectly engineered progressive one, and the two destroy each other the moment they meet. Underneath every worldview, he argues, sits one of two myths: ascent from inferior beings, or descent from superior ones."}, {"title": "Nomad and Settler, Space and Time", "body": "The longest thread of the exclusive hour sets the nomad against the agrarian settler, encoded in Cain and Abel and in Romulus and Remus, where the wall goes up and the wanderer dies for jumping it. Nomads favor the oral arts, animals and space, asking only what they want to do right now. Settlers favor architecture, sculpture and time, forever waiting on planting and harvest and therefore forever convinced the golden age is somewhere else. Mario adds that the nomad is a living axis, like the Fool walking with his pole, while the settler reveres an axis outside himself."}, {"title": "Desire Is the Current of Abundance", "body": "Chance turns the nomad and settler split inward, into the sacral center of the biofield, where value received for creative energy either flows or backs up. People who spend their lives doing what they do not want accumulate frustration there, gradually lose the capacity to feel what they even want, and end up cut off from abundance no matter how hard they work. The actual current in that river, he says, is desire itself. Both men agree the answer is not buying a motorcycle and fleeing, since freedom of movement should follow an internal freedom rather than substitute for it."}, {"title": "The Golden Thread of Baal Keeps Going", "body": "The bull weave never really stops. Chance finds the bull inside diabolos, the Greek word for devil, which reads as god bull once the beta is sounded as a V. Wall and ball share the same swap, since a border exists to contain your Taurus, and polis becomes the place of the bull. Adonis resolves into Adon and nous, lord of the mind, sitting one letter away from Adonai and from adornment. Old English called cattle beeve, Latin called the bee apis, Egypt called its bull god Apis, and Manly Hall's first plate turns out to be crowded with bulls."}]

fields.Plus Quotes JSON: [{"text": "Now in the age of AI, things are moving so fast, it's really hard to keep up, even if you're interested in this kind of stuff.", "author": "Mario Garza", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/94a2fe35-cc60-4591-8931-7e2b7af18c82/MARIO-GARZA.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The way that the perception of time gets throttled up and down has to do with how fast money circulates through an economy, money velocity.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "More than ever, perhaps, this journey to the center of self is maybe more significant.", "author": "Mario Garza", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/94a2fe35-cc60-4591-8931-7e2b7af18c82/MARIO-GARZA.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Even though religious dogmatist types won't want to admit it, the truth is, God is both God and the devil, right?", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The external part of the wheel is related to what's temporary, and then the center of the wheel relates to what is eternal.", "author": "Mario Garza", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/94a2fe35-cc60-4591-8931-7e2b7af18c82/MARIO-GARZA.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Conservatives wanting to uphold tradition, liberals wanting progress for progress's sake. And when those two forces are at odds with each other, it is always destructive, ugly, civilization-ruining.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Tradition, basically, it is like a current. It's almost like a charge, that you're tapping into a current that exists.", "author": "Mario Garza", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/94a2fe35-cc60-4591-8931-7e2b7af18c82/MARIO-GARZA.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "If you conceptualize abundance and receptivity as a flow in a river, the actual flow in that current is desire.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The freedom to move and travel and be wherever is something that should be the result of an internal freedom process that occurs.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "In actuality, it's the center of the wheel, it's the center of the clock that is more primary, and it's more fundamental than what's happening outside of it.", "author": "Mario Garza", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/94a2fe35-cc60-4591-8931-7e2b7af18c82/MARIO-GARZA.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}]
